why: The statement names four conjectures (A/B, C, D, Hodge-type), each over all smooth projective varieties, so any result restricted to a class of varieties or one conjecture is a case. Broe's completion for abelian fourfolds is a case, unreviewed but by a serious method with no identified error, so credible; its disclosure says the model suggested the method and the stabilization idea the proof turns on, which is mathematics in the result, so assisted rather than none. The OpenAI CM manuscript (recorded twice, as openai-cm-hodge-2026 and openai-math-032) gives the Hodge standard conjecture and D for abelian varieties in all characteristics via Milne: a case, unreviewed, doubtful because of the same-release sign-error withdrawals, and generated, since OpenAI is the sole author. Agugliaro 2024 (30 Jan 2024, four days after the snapshot) constructs infinitely many abelian varieties per dimension satisfying the Hodge-type conjecture, not a finite check, so it is a case, digested through Documenta. Foster 2025 and Truong are conditional on open conjectures, so none. Ancona-Marmora's mod-4 signature is a weaker form, so variant. Li's codex credit (strategy exploration, auditing) is too thin to count, and both Li papers are withdrawn anyway. Shimizu has several F10 signals together and is not_credible.
doubts: openai-cm-hodge-2026 and openai-math-032 are one manuscript split into two events; both are answered alike. For the CM paper the per-family generation procedure is not stated in the record (the 032 quote says the CM Hodge work was an exception to the fixed procedure); I took OpenAI's sole authorship as enough for generated. Broe's assisted versus generated was close: the model proposed the method, but the author says they developed, restructured and corrected it. Agugliaro 2024's case-versus-instances call was close: infinitely many explicit examples rather than a complete class.
